newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire TV says price key to Granada bid success.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire TV says price key to Granada bid success.

text.p: Timing and pricing would be key to a successful takeover bid by Britain's Granada Group Plc for Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings, Yorkshire TV said on Sunday.

"The popular conception is that a merger will take place -- it's all down to timing and pricing," a Yorkshire TV spokesperson said in response to a report in the Sunday Times that Granada was close to negotiating a takeover.
Granada has built up a 27 percent stake in Yorkshire TV and has long been expected to mount a takeover bid.

It said on March 13 it had no current intention of bidding for Yorkshire TV, effectively barring itself from making a bid for at least three months, the Sunday Times said. But it noted that the moratorium would expire on Friday.
Yorkshire TV chairman Ward Thomas told Reuters in March that a takeover bid for his company should be pitched as high as 17 pounds a share. The company's shares closed on Friday at 11.07 pounds.
Talks between the two companies resumed after Granada chairman Gerry Robinson and chief executive Charles Allen attended Yorkshire's annual meeting four weeks ago, the Sunday Times said.
Thomas is now on holiday and will return on Thursday, the Yorkshire TV official said, adding his return in advance of the moratorium deadline was not significant.

Separately, Singapore-based DBS Land said its subsidiary, Raffles Holdings, had signed an agreement to buy Brown's Hotel in London from Granada for 45 million pounds (approximately Singapore $105 million).
Also, Sunday Business newspaper said Granada was poised to sell around 30 of its provincial hotels following its takeover last year of Forte.
No one at Granada could be reached for comment.
